pages.text:
Pigsy and Sandy are making dumplings.
Pigsy puts a rectangular bamboo steamer
on the table.
It has ten papers in two rows of five. One
dumpling sits on each paper.
When the steamer is full, it goes on
the stove.
2

Wukong’s job is to carry dumplings from
the cutting board.
Pigsy has already put some in the
first steamer.
“How many more do we need?” asks Pigsy.
Wukong counts from one, but he loses his
place and starts again.
3

“Don’t count the dumplings,” says Sandy.
“Look at the empty papers.”
Wukong looks at the two rows and sees
three empty papers.
“Three are empty, so we need three
more!” he says.
Seven and three make ten.
4

Wukong carries three dumplings from the
board, one at a time.
Now every paper has a dumpling, and the
steamer is full.
Sandy lifts it onto the pot on the stove.
Ten dumplings are cooking, and ten more
wait on the board.
5

Pigsy brings the second steamer with six
dumplings inside.
This time, Wukong does not count
from one.
He looks at the empty papers and
sees four.
“Six and four make ten,” he says, and he
brings four more.
6

Sandy puts the second steamer on top of
the first one.
Then Pigsy brings the third steamer, and
it looks almost full.
Wukong sees only one empty paper
right away.
“Nine and one make ten!” he says, and he
adds one dumpling.
7

Sandy puts the third steamer on
the stack.
Wukong feels quick and proud.
“I don’t need to count from one anymore,”
he says.
“The empty papers tell me how many
more we need.”
8

Pigsy brings the last steamer with eight
dumplings inside.
Five dumplings are left on the board.
“How many is that altogether?”
asks Pigsy.
Eight and five do not make ten, so this
one is harder.
9

Wukong starts to count from one again,
and then he stops.
He looks at the steamer, because the
empty papers helped him before.
Two papers are empty.
“If I move two dumplings, this steamer
will be full,” he says.
10

Wukong moves two dumplings from the
board into the steamer.
Now the steamer has ten, and the board
has three.
Wukong smiles, because no dumplings
went away.
They only moved to a new place.
11

“Ten and three make thirteen!”
says Wukong.
“So eight and five make thirteen, too.”
Pigsy counts them all from one, just to
be sure.
He gets thirteen as well, and he claps
his hands.
12

Sandy puts the last steamer on the stack,
but three dumplings are still on
the board.
Three dumplings cannot fill a steamer.
Pigsy puts them in his little bowl and
says, “This is my three-spot steamer!”
13

Sandy sets Pigsy’s bowl in an empty
steamer on top and puts on the lid.
Soon, warm steam rises from the stack.
It smells so good that Pigsy cannot
sit still.
“We have to wait,” says Sandy.
14

At last, Sandy lifts the lid, and the
dumplings are ready.
Everyone blows on them first, because
they are very hot.
Wukong eats a dumpling from the first
steamer he filled.
Pigsy eats from his three-spot steamer.
15

After lunch, all the papers are empty
again. Wukong looks at a steamer
and laughs.
“Ten empty papers, so we need ten more!”
he says.
Pigsy holds up his bowl and says, “And
three for my three-spot steamer!”
16
